# Compatibility matrix (generated)

**Generated from `docs/compatibility-matrix.json` by `tools/compat-matrix/render.mjs`. Do not edit this file:
edit the JSON and run the generator. `tools/compat-matrix/check.mjs` fails the build when the two differ, when a
cited path or test does not exist, or when a `PASS` row carries an evidence gap.**

Pinned baseline: **SillyTavern 1.19.0**, commit `06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127`.

This matrix is the coarse, capability-level answer to "how far is GoTavern from usable". The per-route
detail lives in `docs/compat-matrix.md` history; this file is the layer that states, per capability area,
what is claimed, what evidences the claim, and — where the claim is short — exactly what is missing.

## Status meanings and counts

| Status | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| PASS | 1 | Every evidence slot the derivation rule requires is present and exists in this tree, and the row carries no evidenceGap. Says nothing about production fitness beyond what the cited evidence covers. |
| PARTIAL | 19 | The mechanism exists and something in this tree gates it, but at least one required evidence slot is missing or a named gap remains. The gap is always named in evidenceGap. |
| FAIL | 1 | A user-visible capability is known to be broken, or the evidence needed to claim it is absent while the defect it would have caught has already shipped. A FAIL row is a finding, not a placeholder. |
| NOT_APPLICABLE | 1 | A decided, recorded exclusion with its reason. Never used for work that is merely unwritten. |

## How a status is derived

Status is derived from what exists in this tree and what the gates actually assert, not from prose. A row is PASS only when every slot below is present AND exists AND evidenceGap is empty; anything else is PARTIAL with the missing slot named, unless a user-visible defect is known, in which case FAIL.

A row is `PASS` only when every one of these holds:

- oracleFixtures: at least one recording of pinned behaviour that the row's differential compares against
- implementation: at least one Go file or package that carries the behaviour
- tests: at least one named test that fails when the behaviour is wrong (existence checked, and the name must resolve to a real test function or harness file)
- ci: at least one workflow job that runs that test
- evidenceGap: empty

**Production rule.** AGENTS.md 22 and 29-30: a behaviour verified only against our own mock peer is `unverified` for production. Such rows cannot be PASS no matter how complete the fixture is, and the gap says so verbatim.

**Artifact rule.** AGENTS.md 23 and 34: a release claim needs the shipped artifact, unpacked, started against a stock tree. Rows whose only evidence is the source tree carry that gap until a release-artifact result exists.

**Fail rule.** AGENTS.md 40: a defect that shipped is recorded here even after it is fixed, because the row's status is about the evidence layer that allowed it through. A fixed mechanism promotes a row from FAIL only when the gate that would have caught it exists and has run.

RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29: FAIL -> PARTIAL. The FAIL was for an absent gate: no test asserted a causala error text for a DNS, connect, TLS, proxy or timeout failure while proving no secret was printed, and every measurement came from a recording peer that cannot produce any of those shapes. Four new peers (untrusted certificate, .invalid host, closed port, 407 proxy) plus the pre-existing stalled-peer test are that gate at the transport, and a shipped-binary test asserts the same taxonomy reaches the browser payload with no credential. The row is PARTIAL rather than PASS because the corpus still runs against our own peer and the live canary needs a credential. CLOSED GAPS, moved out of evidenceGap so that field contains only OPEN gaps: CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE INTERNET-SHAPED GATE. Every production-transport property was asserted against a recording peer that answers HTTP quickly and correctly, so the shapes a real network produces had no test. `internal/outbound/transport_internet_shape_test.go` now drives the PRODUCTION transport against a peer for each failure class, and each assertion is three-part: the error exists, it NAMES the stage and the provider host, and it does NOT contain the request's bearer token. TLS: an untrusted certificate is refused (`TestProductionTransportRefusesAnUntrustedCertificate`). DNS: the RFC 2606 `.invalid` TLD cannot resolve (`TestProductionTransportNamesADNSFailure`). Connect: a port that was just closed refuses (`TestProductionTransportNamesAConnectRefusal`). Proxy: a proxy answering 407 is named as the proxy, not as the provider (`TestProductionTransportNamesAProxyRefusal`). Timeout: a peer that accepts and never answers is attributed to the header stage (`TestProductionTransportAttributesATimeoutToTheHeaderStage`, pre-existing). The connect test's expected wording is deliberately platform-neutral ("connect" + "refused"), because Unix says `connect: connection refused` and Windows says `connectex: ... actively refused it`, and a host-specific phrase would have made the gate untransportable CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THROUGH THE SHIPPED ARTIFACT, which is what AGENTS.md 23 and 35 require. `tests/e2e`'s `TestProviderTransportFailureIsCausalThroughTheShippedBinary` boots the built binary, points a provider's chat URL at a local TLS peer whose certificate cannot chain, drives a real completion through `/api/backends/chat-completions/generate`, and asserts the JSON the browser receives carries `error` exactly as pinned's branch sends it PLUS a `message` that names the TLS stage and contains no credential -- and that the untrusted peer was never reached. THE TEETH WERE OBSERVED: removing the `message` member from `pinnedChatCompletionErrorFlagWithCause` turns it red with `the failure body carries no message, so the user sees no cause (this is the P0-A shape): {"error":true}` (exit 1); the byte copy was restored and the test went green CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE STALE DOCUMENT. `docs/network-egress.md` §2 presented the pre-split `raw.go` measurements as current and is now restated: a status table maps each of D1-D8 to the implementation and the test that would go red, the old table is kept as HISTORY with a banner saying it is superseded, and a paragraph names what is still NOT proven (the differential corpus still runs against our own recording peer)

**Evidence gap**: none.

Blocked by: `providers-transport`

Streaming has the deepest browser instrumentation in the tree (frame-by-frame render alignment on both legs). The network half has its own artefact (tests/browser/streaming-framing-comparison.json) with a real TCP hop behind it, and that artefact is now GREEN and gate-checked: browser-differential.yml run 40682654579 passed the comparator (step 16) with both subjects reporting the same partial text. THE CUT FIRES AT A BYTE OFFSET ON A FRAME BOUNDARY, not timed against the page: framesToBytes(3) = 513 of the peer's 2,565 bytes, so both subjects deliver and render content before the cut -- measured contentStates 2, textAfterCut "Hello from the", releasedBytes 349, plaintextOffsetAtCut 513, identically on both. The earlier reasoning is retained because it is WHY the cut point is a frame boundary: a cut INSIDE a record leaves both frontends before their error path with zero content states (measured, runs 40316734219, 40322630841, 40324760750), and a head-of-body cut delivers no body at all, so neither produces partial text to compare. The head-of-body vehicle this row previously cited as PROVEN (run 40331271988) is superseded and retired. Buffering-proxy mode is a DECIDED EXCLUSION, not a gap: a hop that releases the whole body in ONE write makes the number of rendered states a function of the browser commit schedule rather than of the server (measured 2 on GoTavern and 1 on pinned, run 40299346339), so that mode was deleted and its claim is NOT made. Status stays PARTIAL on the two surviving gaps below -- the TLS-close gap and the absent ordering gate -- not on inertia: the network half is proven, the row is not. RE-DERIVED 2026-10-29: the two remaining gaps are closed by committed tests (a graceful TLS shutdown mid-frame, and the frame-ORDER property for a complete and a cancelled stream), and the row's browser instrumentation was already green and gate-checked, so the row carries no evidence gap and is PASS rather than PARTIAL. The buffering-proxy mode stays a DECIDED EXCLUSION in this row's notes, which is a decision and not a gap. CLOSURE RECORD (kept out of evidenceGap because a PASS row may not carry gaps): CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- MID-STREAM TLS CLOSE. The row said the fault 'is a socket close on plain HTTP' and that a TLS fatal alert was not reproduced; the first half was STALE (TestProductionTransportSurfacesAMidStreamCloseCausally already starts a TLS server and hijacks the connection), and the second half is now covered in BOTH directions: an ABRUPT close (existing test) and a GRACEFUL TLS shutdown mid-frame, where the server hijacks its `*tls.Conn` and closes it properly so a close_notify goes out. `TestProductionTransportTreatsAGracefulTLSShutdownMidStreamAsTruncation` requires that case to reach the caller as an ERROR (a silent success would show half an answer as a complete one), that the bytes that DID arrive are still delivered, that the error is classifiable (unexpected EOF / truncation / closed / reset) and that it carries no credential. Teeth observed: returning `io.EOF` instead of the mid-stream error turns it red with 'a provider that shut the TLS session down mid-frame produced NO error' CLOSED 2026-10-29 -- THE ORDERING PROPERTY, ASSERTED AS A PROPERTY RATHER THAN AS A RECORDED PARTIAL TEXT. `TestProductionTransportPreservesProviderFrameOrder` makes a provider write 200 distinguishable SSE frames one per write, with a flush after each so they arrive in separate reads, then requires the received bytes to equal the sent bytes AND the parsed frame indices to be 0..199 in order with none dropped or duplicated. The row claim is now MEASURED rather than inferred: eight steps, eight experiments is replaced by one session per subject, and the surface found a concrete provider-context difference on its first run with green legs — which is what this row was for. It stays FAIL because a user first request reaching the model with different example dialogue than pinned is a parity defect, not evidence debt. The finding above is the next change whole brief: record the example-dialogue block as the page holds it at first load and after the reload, and diff it against the served card payload, per subject.

## The whole-session differential (what exists today)

The whole-session differential AGENTS.md 34/38 asks for NOW EXISTS as tests/browser/whole-session-probe.mjs + compare-whole-session-legs.mjs, gated by whole-session.yml#whole-session, and its first run (41015209900) was red for a real first-turn provider-context difference: see row `whole-session-e2e`. The step table below is the PREVIOUS per-surface inventory it subsumes and is retained because those probes are still each surface’s evidence. `sharedFixture` stays false and the row stays FAIL until a fresh green run at the candidate SHA exists, because `tools/compat-matrix/check.mjs` refuses a FAIL row that asserts a shared session.

- State carried between steps: **true**
- One shared runtime/fixture across steps: **false**
- Harness reused: `tools/probe-*.mjs`, `tests/browser/generation-probe.mjs`, `tests/browser/capture-preset.mjs`

| Step | What the user does | Probe | Both legs compared | Shares runtime with other steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| load | open the pinned frontend root in a browser | `tools/probe-frontend-static.mjs` | true | false |
| settings | read and save settings | `tools/probe-settings-save.mjs` | true | false |
| characters | list and open a character | `tools/probe-characters-read.mjs` | true | false |
| open-chat | open a chat and see its history | `tools/probe-chats-save-get.mjs` | true | false |
| send | send a message and receive a completion | `tools/probe-provider-wire.mjs` | true | false |
| stream | send with streaming on, then cancel mid-stream | `tests/browser/generation-probe.mjs` | true | false |
| save | save the chat | `tools/probe-chats-mutations.mjs` | true | false |
| reload | reload the page and see the conversation back | _not implemented_: no probe reads state back through the frontend after a reload; chats-save-get compares the HTTP round trip, not the browser's rehydration | false | false |

**Canonicalisation.** Each step's observation is compared after replacing those four classes with markers by FIELD PATH, never by regex over the whole document, and the replacement is recorded beside the observation so it cannot be silently widened. Byte equality is never claimed for a field that carries a clock.

Replaced per field path, never by whole-document regex: `timestamps`, `nonces and session ids`, `ports`, `absolute host paths`.

Forbidden: dropping whole response bodies; sorting arrays whose order is the contract; ignoring status codes.
